GTA 6 Will Do Something the Franchise Has Never Done Before: Encourage Empathy
items.summary: Rockstar has confirmed GTA 6 features something the franchise has never had before: mechanisms that encourage

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/05/jason-and-lucia-14-1793891731334.jpg
Rockstar has confirmed GTA 6 features something the franchise has never had before: mechanisms that encourage empathy.

Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson and head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe talked about how next week's Grand Theft Auto changes the formula the series is known for during an interview with The Guardian (via @GameRoll_ ). Jason and Lucia will surely be able to cause a fair amount of chaos when players take control in Vice City, but in a post- Red Dead Redemption 2 world, they'll have the freedom to be kind, too.

"Crime is a fundamental part of GTA – at least up until now, it has been," Nelson said. "We're trying to make sure we're not punishing people for playing the game they are used to … [but] your actions will have some effect on how the game plays out."

Games like GTA 5 have given players playgrounds and characters that can maximize the mayhem. Trevor, one of that game's three protagonists, is a great example of this chaotic energy, but in GTA 6, there doesn't seem to be a direct equivalent. Sure, Rockstar's trademark tone and instantly recognizable characters can be seen all over what few trailers we've received thus far, but everything seems a bit more grounded, too.

Falling in line with this is the news that GTA 6 will feature a world that might actually reward those who take the citizens of Leonida into consideration. Of course, that doesn't mean those who prefer to wreak havoc won't be able to play their way, too. It just means that, at least based on Nelson's words, there's some room to be a normal or even good person, too.

"I would say so," he replied when asked if the new game would encourage empathy in some capacity. "I would say that it's a product of the story we're trying to tell. We've tried for the first time in a GTA to provide mechanisms that encourage it, for those who want to."

Elsewhere in the interview, Nelson described Jason and Lucia as a "younger couple with their backs against the wall," which is why it doesn't make sense for them to "go out and cause as much carnage and make as much noise as they can." This isn't Michael, Franklin, or Trevor, nor is it Niko Bellic. Thankfully, we won't have to wait too much longer to find out just what kind of criminals Jason and Lucia are, or who they can be.

GTA 6 launches November 19, 2026, for PS5 and Xbox Series X | S. With more grounded in-game mechanisms and NPCs that react to weapons, it's clear we're staring down what will likely be the most realistic Grand Theft Auto game so far. It's something that has plenty of fans excited and others nervous . Recent footage shared by Rockstar has highlighted the game's unbelievable graphics . It's something that has IGN writer Jacqueline Thomas excited , even if it does run at 30 fps .

items.title: 您喜欢老式 MMO 中的生物标记，还是已经厌倦了为任务积分而战？

content.v: https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/PgGhmt5pTtxusaQQX3dHPF-1920-80.png

This is Terminally Online : PC Gamer's very own MMO column. Every other week, I'll be sharing my thoughts on the genre, interviewing fellow MMO-heads like me, taking a deep-dive into mechanics we've all taken for granted, and, occasionally, bringing in guest writers to talk about their MMO of choice.

I've been having a pleasant time with WoW: Forever (and by that, I mean it has consumed nearly every waking moment of my life). One thing, however, has been made pretty clear: Mob tagging, that is, only giving kill credit to the first player (or group) to damage a mob, is divisive.

One side of the fence—my side, I'm afraid—does see mob tagging as a necessary evil in an MMO that's trying to drive social interaction. Videogames, particularly ones that are incentivising you to group up, are kind of meant to be a pain in the butt sometimes; if you've got a "kill 20" quest and there another person there, the fact you might get in each other's way if you don't group up, and have a jollier time if you do, is a net good.

I have more complicated thoughts on item drop quests being bad in a group, sure. And I'd like it if Blizzard's layering technology was a little more merciful. But, overall, I'm all for it. Nearly every single person I've thrown an invite to has grouped up with me, and I've even (gasp) had conversations with strangers. Pleasant ones!

Some of them are even on my friends list now, and it is, I think, a point in my favour that I would have largely ignored every single person I am now regularly chatting to if mob tagging wasn't a thing.

However, I do get the other side of the fence, in that it is absolutely a pain in the ass. Particularly in a game that's just launched, where the playerbase is nowhere near as spread out as it needs to be. There's a thin difference between good social banter being encouraged and "for the love of god, I just need one troll fetish, why are these mystics spread 30 feet apart, thank god I farmed my mount before I did this".

A difference, it's important to state, that is more often broken in a game that's so wildly popular as Forever is right now. Mob tagging holds up when it's you and a handful of other players in a questing environment: It's less defensible when there's 30 of you and it's a "loot X" quest so grouping wouldn't help, anyway.
So I ask you, fine readers of Terminally Online: Do you think tagging mobs is fine in an oldschool MMO, or is it an archaic thing of the past to be done away with?
If you've got deeper thoughts on this, let me know in the comments below!

items.title: 《匕首之心：希望与恐惧》扩展包评测

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/13/hopeandfear-thumb-1794603742410.jpg
Critical Role 的 TTRPG 系统 Daggerheart 比其他同类系统更加注重故事讲述。核心书发布一年后，Daggerheart 通过系统的首次扩展为玩家和游戏大师提供了讲述故事的新选择。
作为一个在 GM 屏幕两侧玩各种角色扮演游戏的人，我总是渴望有更多的选择。更多的装备可供我的英雄使用，更多的恶毒怪物可以攻击我毫无戒心的玩家。
《匕首之心：希望与恐惧》在玩具箱中添加了大量玩具，但如果您不是核心书的粉丝，请不要指望此扩展包会改变您的想法。
在深入了解新内容之前，对于那些不熟悉的人来说，《Daggerheart》是一款以叙事为中心的桌面角色扮演游戏系统。它使用一种相当方便的基于卡片的方法来帮助创建和管理你的角色，并在战斗中废除传统的主动机制。然而，《匕首之心》最具决定性的机制之一是它的希望和恐惧骰子。
这两个十二面骰子，一个代表你的希望值，另一个代表恐惧，可以让你的支票为你赢得“希望”资源，可用于完成额外的特殊行动，或者给你的GM一个他们可以花费的“恐惧”点。一种众所周知的“齿轮扳手”之类的款待，具体取决于检查过程中哪个骰子滚动得更高。该机制也与该系统的第一个扩展包同名。
哪里购买
《匕首之心：希望与恐惧》扩展包可在关键角色商店购买，售价 39.99 美元。

For players who have been wanting to make some new characters, a plethora of options await you inside this nearly 200-page tome. The Hope and Fear expansion comes with four new classes, each with two subclasses, six ancestries and communities, over 100 new pieces of gear and loot to dig through, and a brand-new domain. GMs get some new toys too, with 130+ new enemies to sic on those pesky heroes across 28 environments and four campaign frames (think of these as rough bases to build a campaign around). By far, though, my personal favorite inclusion in H&F is the brand-new Transformations system, but more on that gem in a bit.

The new domain, Dread, actually has some pretty interesting effects. The ones I found most intriguing and beneficial were abilities like Avatar of Terror, which makes you stronger the more Fear the GM has, and the spell Dire-Strike, which straight-up takes some of the GM’s Fear away. The idea that my friends and I could gang up and shut down the bullshit my GM might pull during a game instantly shot this new Domain to the top of my list for the next character I make.

Two new classes, the Assassin (a standalone, more stabby-focused rogue) and the Brawler (Daggerheart’s punchy monk-like class), utilize the core domains that came in the core book, while the other two new classes, the Warlock (make a pact with a thing, get cool powers) and the Witch (mess with enemies by hexing them), take advantage of H&F’s new Dread domain.
对于《D&D》玩家来说，新的祖先基本上相当于《Daggerheart》中的物种，任何玩过其他高奇幻 TTRPG 的人都会感到熟悉。以太族是有翅膀的天使生物，而元素亲属——由土族、灰烬族（火）、天空族和潮汐族（水）组成——是强大元素的后代。然后还有侏儒，嗯，侏儒。
拥有一切当然很好，但新血统和一些新类别似乎都是核心幻想主食，以至于我觉得很奇怪它们没有包含在基础版本中。不过，很高兴他们现在在这里，侏儒能够利用他们的闪烁步功能进行传送，这真是太有趣了。
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/13/hopeandfear-review-2-1794603742409.jpg

对于永远的游戏大师（你们是真正的英雄）来说，希望与恐惧的新战役框架为犹豫不决的全新玩家或想要挑战的白发老兵提供了良好的游戏运行灵活性。令人惊讶的是，四个产品中我最喜欢的也是最不复杂的：Castle High。想想现代的巫师学校，青少年们骑着扫帚飞来飞去，一边滚动手机，一边在空中巨大的浮岛上上课。虽然我还没有玩过或运行过这个框架，但把我的剑换成铅笔和纸，偷偷溜出学校而不是地牢，这个想法是一个有趣的节奏变化。
当然，如果你想杀死一条龙，或者在本例中是杀死一个狼人龙暴君，你也可以在《狼人之治》中做到这一点。最复杂的新游戏《地平线之旅》要求你努力复活女神。

Now we can get to my favorite addition: transformations. Becoming a demigod, a werewolf, a vampire, or even living out your Danny Phantom dreams by transforming into a ghost is now possible! All of the transformation options in H&F (of which there are six) come with some sort of bonus or ability in addition to a downside. In Danny Phantom’s case, you take less physical damage but double magic damage, and can pass through solid objects at the cost of taking on some Stress.

I love transformations as a way to add further depth of your character or as a narrative plot thread, and the fact that they don’t count against any sort of domain or character limit (outside of only being allowed a single transformation at a time, but that’s what house rules are for) opens up all sorts of possibilities. Now, if Darrington Press could just make an official Super Sentai / Power Ranger transformation equivalent, I’d be all set! Castle High already features teenagers with attitude as the player characters, after all.
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/13/hopeandfear-review-3-1794603742409.jpg

Daggerheart: Hope & Fear is a good first expansion, though it feels like a safe one. It adds a fair amount of new content for both players and GMs to mess around with, which is always great, even if some additions feel like they should have been included from the start. The Dread domain and how it can mess with the GM’s plans directly is a really fun twist. I’ve already gushed about the transformations, and I can’t wait to see what new options get added down the road.
话虽如此，自推出以来，《Daggerheart》对于那些不习惯即兴创作和叙述自己正在做的事情的人来说，感觉是一款更加令人生畏的游戏，而《希望与恐惧》对此并没有真正的帮助。我喜欢它所添加的内容，但如果你已经被核心游戏淹没了，请不要指望这个扩展包来拯救你。相对而言，Daggerheart 作为一个系统仍处于起步阶段，我希望看到一个精心组合的入门套件或更多手持式扩展包来帮助新玩家上手。

items.title: I summoned 1 blood demon, stitched 2 of my disciples together, and seduced 3 snails in this excellent cult simulator in the spirit of Dwarf Fortress
items.summary: World's Best Grandpa Cup be praised.

content.v: Weird Weekend is our regular Saturday column where we celebrate PC gaming oddities: peculiar games, strange bits of trivia, forgotten history. Pop back every weekend to find out what Jeremy, Josh, Rick and Ted have become obsessed with this time, whether it's the canon height of Thief's Garrett or that time someone in the Vatican pirated Football Manager .

What's the fastest you've ever fallen in love with a game? I think I have a new record: about 0.3 seconds into CultGame , when launching it from Steam spawned not a regular game window, but a command prompt instance. Perfection. Chef's kiss. No notes.

Like the Bay 12 games (Dwarf Fortress and especially Liberal Crime Squad ) it clearly takes inspiration from, CultGame is gloriously text-based. Its art is ASCII, its options selected by tippy-tapping the numpad, its maps are carpets of symbols: lurid at signs and hashes as far as the eye can see.

It's a management game, first and foremost. Once you have generated a world and a history for it, you choose the precise nature of cult leader you wish to be: Defector Cleric, Occult Scholar, Con Artist, or Lunatic, and off you go. I was Gideon Faircloth, the fallen cleric, and my object of reverence was a 'World's Best Grandpa' Cup whose domains were blood and fire.

CultGame lets you rewrite basically everything, including the deity type you follow; it does not protest, I learnt, when you write some absolute nonsense in there. I learnt this lesson again when the game asked me to choose a creed for my nascent faith and I wrote "Opinions are not those of my employer".

Like Dwarf Fortress, CultGame will procedurally gin up an entire worldmap for you at the game's start and speckle it with locations of interest. There are barren plains and thick, unpeopled woodlands aplenty, but also dense urban spaces, pre-existing religions, political factions and more, all just waiting for you to get in there and start corrupting the populace. As a former preacher, I already had some skill points in preaching, so on turn one I set up shop in an area the game had named "The Friendly Wilds of Evil" to begin hollering at the hoi polloi.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/cVCvYAXS7tSiQ4p7kwfWXA-1920-80.jpg

My charisma and probably-airtight cup-centric theology quickly won the crowd's adoration. Before long, I was accruing ~60 followers a turn. As the masses converted, they began generating followers themselves like a religious Roth IRA. Before long, I had my first recruit—not just a passive follower, but someone I could directly control and recruit just like Gideon. He was called Leopold Blackwood and he soon got to preaching, doubling my monthly followers. Soon, a new recruit, more preaching, more followers, and so on.

The tithes I was extracting from the rubes gathered in mountains. I had closets full of gold, and before long I was initiating grand public works in the areas of my preaching—shrines and gardens about town that made me look very generous indeed. Even the indigenous religion didn't mind me so much: when its apostles had challenged my preaching, I succeeded in a skill check that made them rather like me. I was munificent and popular—a beloved figure.
It was time to start killing people.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/334FQE9yhjqYJqertYExZA-1920-80.jpg

One of the labours you can set your cult minions about in CultGame's demo is ritual-making. Depending on your deity's chosen domain, you get access to a set of thematically appropriate magic tricks you can expend resources to cast. Our World's Best Grandpa Cup started off as a blood-domain deity and added fire when we got enough followers to branch out. This meant our cardinals were very good at reworking the flesh of man and could, if you catch them in the right mood, raze a city with a targeted meteor strike.

So we got about doing that, mostly just to see what would happen. Our flesh rituals were powered by blood, which meant we had to induct some recruits we might normally have turned away due to their poor stats and start converting them to non-renewable energy. I put a recruit named Isabella in charge of the abattoir; her ritual-casting ability trumped everyone else's. She did a great job. Well done, Isabel. Everyone say well done Isabel.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/BwjsnLXbmPsXfLrQPptDSA-1920-80.jpg

Before long I had converted two underperforming cultists named John and Sarah into a single, flesh-joined creature named Jorah the Grafted, who met expectations. Isabel also summoned a blood demon, a new employee named Morfangrag whose stats were off-the-charts good to the extent that it made everyone else in the cult look like additional potential fleshgrafting candidates. Morfangrag was incredibly useful, and would not kill us so long as he got a monthly dose of blood, which was fine: we still had plenty of low-quality recruits knocking on our door looking to sign up.

Things were going very well, but I had yet to check out the demo's Crusade feature, whereby you can dispatch a follower or followers to set heathen areas aflame with the light of the true faith. I sent Morfangrag to a cave. He easily dispatched the skeletons, spiders, and so on within. And yet…
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Hghc5bKCs3kQoEyu6JwzZA-1920-80.jpg

Just before Morfangrag set out, the cult of the World's Best Grandpa Cup levelled up to the point that it could adopt a new belief. I picked the one that let us speak to animals. Possessed of a perhaps religious vision, I sidled Morfangrag up to an escargatoire of three snails and hit the Flirt option.

My blood demon successfully charmed all three snails, who collectively became his girlfriend and, thereby, minions of the cult. They didn't even mind that he took them on (free) dates to the local dump instead of (expensive) dates to a fancy restaurant. They were into it, if anything.
Anyway, they were all eventually sacrificed to fuel some more fleshgrafting. CultGame is a very good time.

items.title: 迷你评论：Tape To Tape (Switch) - 一款适合服务不足的曲棍球爱好者的 Roguelite 游戏
items.summary: Accept Fight! (L+R). If you are a hockey fan with a Switch, you have been poorly served by the system’s librar

content.v: Accept Fight! (L+R).

If you are a hockey fan with a Switch, you have been poorly served by the system’s library. Odd really, considering how well hockey itself translates into video game form. And then you chance upon T ape to Tape drowning in the weekly AI slop eShop releases, a curiously labelled “gorgeous roguelite hockey world" affair. Is this it? Is this the hockey game of my dreams?

Tape to Tape did not sprout magically overnight. It has been a labour of love for several years and has been feeding off a lively player community with feedback to shape the version now in our hands. Forget about offsides, penalties, and other obtuse rules (unless you pick the Modern Squad): this is hardcore old-school hockey the likes of which we haven't seen since NHL Hitz and that is a very good thing indeed.
Read the full article on nintendolife.com
